foundation:finite-lp-strong-duality.contract: A feasible finite-dimensional linear program with finite optimum has an equal dual optimum under the stated primal/dual formulation.

root:gottesman-stabilizer-formalism.contract: An abelian Pauli subgroup not containing -I defines its common +1 eigenspace; the rank-n, k=0 case defines a pure stabilizer state.
root:gottesman-stabilizer-formalism.artifact: Reference/Stabilizer Codes and Quantum Error Correction/Thesis.tex

root:howard-campbell-rom.contract: RoM is the minimum l1 norm of a signed affine decomposition over pure stabilizer states; RoM=1 exactly on the stabilizer polytope and is nonincreasing under stabilizer operations.
root:howard-campbell-rom.artifact: Reference/Application of a resource theory for magic states to fault-tolerant quantum computing/Robustness_main_appendix.tex

root:perfect-graph-weighted-duality.contract: For a finite perfect graph and nonnegative weights, the maximum-weight stable-set value equals the fractional clique-cover optimum. This equality contract does not itself include an algorithmic complexity claim.

root:varela-reduced-polytope.contract: A Pauli expectation window defines a projected stabilizer polytope and reduced RoM; its claimed V-representation uses maximal commuting contexts and admissible signs.
root:varela-reduced-polytope.artifact: Reference/Predicting magic from very few measurements/pra_version.tex

root:veitch-stabilizer-resource-theory.contract: Pure stabilizer states form a finite Clifford orbit; the full free state set STAB is their convex hull; states not freely preparable are magic/nonstabilizer resources, and stabilizer operations are free operations.
root:veitch-stabilizer-resource-theory.artifact: Reference/The Resource Theory of Stabilizer Computation/stab_resource_theory_021.tex

claim:full-rom.contract: Full RoM is the minimum l1 norm of a signed affine decomposition of rho over pure stabilizer states, with value one exactly on STAB_n.

claim:full-stabilizer-polytope.contract: STAB_n is the convex hull of all pure n-qubit stabilizer states.

claim:pauli-window.contract: A finite set M of nonidentity Hermitian n-qubit Pauli observables maps rho to b_M(rho)=(tr(P rho))_{P in M}.

claim:frustration-graph.contract: G_M has one vertex per measured Pauli and an edge exactly for anticommuting pairs; independent sets are pairwise commuting contexts.

claim:reduced-rom.contract: RoM_M(rho) is the minimum l1 norm of a signed affine decomposition of b_M(rho) over STAB(M); projection implies RoM_M(rho)<=RoM(rho), so RoM_M(rho)>1 is a sound magic certificate. With M held fixed, it is not a monotone under all stabilizer operations.

claim:reduced-stabilizer-polytope.contract: STAB(M) is the image of STAB_n under the Pauli expectation window.

claim:dependency-affine-code.contract: Within a commuting context, phase-free kernel relations with their +/- identity syndromes are exactly the parity checks defining the admissible sign assignments.

claim:exact-reduced-vrep.contract: STAB(M)=conv{v_(S,f)} over inclusion-maximal commuting contexts S and phase-aware admissible signs f.

claim:mwis-definition.contract: For nonnegative vertex weights w, alpha_w(G) is the maximum total weight over all independent sets of G.

claim:perfect-graph-definition.contract: G is perfect iff every induced subgraph G' satisfies chromatic_number(G')=clique_number(G').

claim:relaxed-rom.contract: relaxed_RoM_M is the minimum l1 signed affine decomposition of b_M(rho) over the sign-relaxed polytope.

claim:sign-relaxed-polytope.contract: The sign-relaxed polytope retains all +/- assignments on every maximal commuting context, including assignments not compatible with Pauli product relations.

claim:sign-syndrome-linear-consistent.contract: For commuting Hermitian Pauli representatives, the product phase defines a linear syndrome on ker(M_S); independent generator eigenvalues extend consistently, so B_S is a nonempty affine coset of size 2^rank(M_S).

claim:pauli-active-dependency.contract: An inclusion-minimal Pauli product relation is active exactly when its support is pairwise commuting and therefore imposes a joint-eigenvalue parity check.

claim:relaxed-affine-span.contract: For every measured coordinate i, a maximal commuting context containing i and a one-sign flip yield a vertex difference proportional to e_i; hence the relaxed primal is feasible for every b in R^m and bounded below by one.

claim:no-active-free-signs.contract: M has no Pauli-active dependency iff every commuting context admits every deterministic sign assignment.

claim:perfect-graph-antiblocker.contract: For a perfect graph, {z>=0:alpha_z<=1} is the convex hull of clique incidence vectors including the empty clique. The target derives this locally from weighted stable-set/fractional-cover duality and downward closure.

claim:relaxed-lp-dual.contract: Strong LP duality turns relaxed RoM into a maximization over (y,mu) with one absolute-value constraint per relaxed vertex.

claim:sign-alignment-identity.contract: For fixed S,y,mu, maximizing over all sign assignments gives sum_{i in S}|y_i|+|mu|.

claim:relaxation-exactness.contract: STAB(M) equals the sign-relaxed polytope iff M has no Pauli-active dependency; in that regime exact and relaxed reduced RoM coincide.

claim:relaxed-mwis-dual.contract: relaxed_RoM_M(rho)=max b.y+mu subject to alpha_|y|(G_M)+|mu|<=1; a maximum-weight independent set supplies a violated constraint when one exists.

claim:exact-graph-program.contract: Under no Pauli-active dependency, the MWIS-constrained relaxed dual is the exact reduced-RoM dual.

claim:closed-form-rom.contract: If M has no Pauli-active dependency and G_M is perfect, RoM_M(rho)=max(1,max_Q sum_{P in Q}|tr(P rho)|).
